finalists.label: Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome
finalists.why: It has specific evidence of compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle.

finalists.label: Gastrointestinal Obstruction
finalists.why: It is a broad category that encompasses the patient's symptoms of intractable vomiting, inability to tolerate oral intake, and marked gastric distension.

finalists.label: Roux-en-Y Stenosis
finalists.why: It is not well-supported due to the lack of intrinsic luminal lesions and normal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, but it is still considered due to marked gastric distension.

frontier_selector.why: The champion is chosen because it has the most specific evidence, including compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta at an acute angle, which directly explains the patient's symptoms.
